startup.definition: A young company developing a new product or business idea.

founder.definition: A person who starts a company or organization.

co-founder.definition: A person who starts a company or organization together with one or more other people.

ceo.definition: The corporate executive responsible for the operations of the firm.

cto.definition: A chief technology officer, meaning a senior executive responsible for an organization’s technology direction.

mvp.definition: Minimum viable product: an early usable version for testing an idea with customers.

pitch-deck.definition: A short presentation that explains a business, product, problem, solution, market, and plan to an audience such as investors or partners.
pitch-deck.exampleUsage: The team revised the pitch deck before the competition.

business-plan.definition: A document explaining a business's goals and how it intends to achieve them.

mission-statement.definition: A concise statement explaining an organization’s purpose and what it aims to do.

vision.definition: An idea of what an organization hopes to achieve in the future.

seed-round.definition: An early stage of startup financing used to support initial development and growth.
seed-round.exampleUsage: The startup raised a seed round to develop and test its first product.

series-a.definition: An early major funding round for a startup that has begun developing its business.

angel-investor.definition: A private individual who invests in a young company, usually in exchange for an ownership interest.

venture-capital.definition: Investment in young or growing companies by specialist investors or funds, usually in exchange for ownership interests.

crowdfunding.definition: Raising funds from many backers, often through an online platform, under stated project terms.

bootstrap.definition: To build a business using the founders' own resources and income.

valuation.definition: An estimate of a company’s financial value under stated assumptions.

equity.definition: An ownership share in a company.

dilution.arabicTranslation: انخفاض نسبة الملكية بسبب إصدار حصص جديدة
dilution.definition: A decrease in an owner's share when a company issues more shares.

term-sheet.definition: A document outlining the main proposed terms of a business investment or financial agreement before final contracts are completed.
term-sheet.exampleUsage: The founders reviewed the term sheet with qualified legal advisers.

traction.definition: Evidence that customers are using or buying a startup's product.

user-acquisition.definition: The process of attracting and gaining new users or customers for a product or service.
user-acquisition.exampleUsage: The startup measured the cost of user acquisition.

retention.definition: A business's ability to keep customers or users over time.

churn-rate.definition: The percentage of customers or users who stop using a service during a given period.
churn-rate.exampleUsage: The team tracks churn rate each month.

growth-hacking.definition: A business term for rapid, experimental methods aimed at increasing users, engagement, or revenue, often with limited resources.
growth-hacking.exampleUsage: The marketing team tested a growth-hacking experiment and measured its results.

product-market-fit.definition: A situation in which a product strongly meets the needs of a real target market and customers consistently value it.
product-market-fit.exampleUsage: The founders interviewed customers while testing product-market fit.

pivot.definition: To change a business strategy in response to what has been learned.

scale.definition: To grow a business so it can serve more customers or handle more work.
scale.exampleUsage: The founders planned to scale the service after testing demand and capacity.

runway.definition: The time a company can keep operating before its available cash runs out.

burn-rate.definition: The rate at which a company spends available cash over a period, especially before it becomes profitable.
burn-rate.exampleUsage: The financial model tracks the startup's monthly burn rate.

disrupt.definition: To change an industry by introducing a new way of doing things.

iterate.definition: To improve a product through repeated cycles of testing and revision.

lean.arabicTranslation: قائم على تقليل الهدر واختبار الافتراضات
lean.definition: Using limited resources efficiently while testing ideas quickly.

agile.definition: Using short cycles of development and adapting to feedback.

sprint.definition: A short period of focused work to complete a set of tasks.

standup.definition: A short team meeting to discuss progress and immediate work, often traditionally held standing.

retrospective.definition: A team meeting to review past work and decide how to improve.

okr.definition: Objectives and Key Results, a goal-setting method that pairs a clear objective with measurable results used to track progress.
okr.exampleUsage: The team set an OKR for improving customer response time.

north-star.definition: A main measure used to guide a company's progress.

unicorn.definition: A privately held startup valued at one billion US dollars or more.
unicorn.arabicTranslation: شركة ناشئة خاصة قيمتها مليار دولار أو أكثر
